question: The department lists "belief state epidemiology". If a belief spreads among 14 agents, how much does one run differ from the deterministic epidemic curve?
production_path: investigation: read the department record, the 21 belief files and the two record types the repository defines for an agent's beliefs (belief snapshot, knowledge state) at the pinned commit; took over an interrupted extract script, kept its blob checks and added a shape test over the JSON files under state/
extract: snapshot the department's wording, one row per belief file and the result of the shape test into observed-input.json, refusing any source file or scanned file set that differs from the pin
model: SIR with uniform mixing applied to a belief as an analogy; deterministic curve and final-size equation; embedded jump chain for the stochastic model, so that no waiting time is drawn

test: 10,000 seeded runs for each of six cases (14 and 1,400 agents; R0 = 4/5, 6/5 and 3; one initial holder), the exact final-size distribution by summation over the jump chain, and the comparison with the deterministic final size and the branching-process value

adversarial: agreement test against counts simulated with another reproduction number, planted second holder of a proposition, sample files as a positive control of the shape test, and the objection that a broadcast from a common source fits the repository's samples as well as contagion does
test: byte-identical reruns under Python 3.9, 3.12 and 3.14 on Windows and under Linux, self-checks that abort the run, five answered exercises and an answer-free transfer task

revision after an independent reading of the draft (not a human subject review), which reproduced the model part by another route and found the draft's claim that the repository records no transmission contradicted by two belief files: reread those two files, the script that writes them, the message schema and the recommendation folder at the pin; the extract now counts the belief files whose evidence names a contract message, scans the JSON files under state/ for a key that would name a sender and separates belief files with content from empty scaffolds; a fixed-holding-time contrast was added to the branching value; 42 self-checks, and the reruns repeated on the same four interpreters
hypothesis: As stated in the module notes before any run: with one initial holder among 14 agents, the number of agents that ever hold the belief follows a wide, two-humped distribution and the deterministic epidemic curve describes neither hump; among 1,400 agents the share of runs that fade out early is close to the branching-process value 1/R0 when R0 exceeds 1.
evidence: Observed at Demerzel commit 4b03838800dcd4894f1e026461979bff1d985ca8: the department record lists "Belief state epidemiology — how beliefs spread across agents and repos" as research area 7 of 10; of the 21 belief files (8 current, 13 archived) the 12 with content have one evaluator, Demerzel, and the other 9 are empty scaffolds, so finding no proposition under two holders could not have shown sharing; two current files (confidence-calibration, remediation-effectiveness) each rest on one ml-feedback-recommendation message whose rationale and confidence a script of the repository copies into Demerzel's belief, and since the two messages are not in the repository, that they came from ix's ML pipeline rests on the schema's description and the script's docstring. Those are two adoptions from a document, as the broadcast objection expects; none of the 722 JSON files under state/ (course library excluded) has the shape of a belief snapshot or of a knowledge state, or a key naming a teacher, a learner or a message's sender (origin_repo, origin_agent), so no file read records a holder passing a belief on, a second hop or an agent exposed without adopting: no rate can be estimated and the model is untested on the project.

Synthetic, 14 agents, 10,000 seeded runs per reproduction number: at R0 = 3 the final size has two humps (2,664 runs end at 1 agent, 4,192 at 13 or 14), but the deterministic final size 13.24 lies inside the upper hump, with 5,001 runs within 1.4 agents of it. At R0 = 1.2 and R0 = 0.8 the exact distribution has a single hump at 1 agent (4,706 and 5,708 runs), and only 992 runs end within 1.4 agents of the deterministic 6.65 at R0 = 1.2.

Synthetic, 1,400 agents: at R0 = 3, 3,366 of 10,000 runs end at or below 140 agents (exact probability 0.3339; branching value 1/3, which rests on the model's exponential holding time: a fixed one would give 0.0595) and 6,634 end within 140 agents of the deterministic 1,316.74, with no run between 16 and 1,256 agents. At R0 = 1.2, 8,455 runs end at or below 140 (exact 0.8459 against a branching value of 0.8333, and the share moves with the cut) and 1,097 within 140 agents of the deterministic 443.03.

Checks: in all six cases the simulated counts stay within 2.65 binomial standard errors of the exact jump-chain probabilities, counts simulated at R0 = 3 are rejected against the exact R0 = 1.2 distribution, the integrated curve ends within 1e-6 of the root of the final-size equation, and the results were byte-identical under Python 3.9, 3.12 and 3.14 on Windows and 3.14 on Linux.

The hypothesis is contradicted in its first half (two humps appear only at R0 = 3, and there the curve does describe the upper one) and supported in its second half at R0 = 3. No rate was estimated from project data, only SIR with uniform mixing was tried, and when this record was written (2026-10-13), no human subject review, learner trial, translation or publication of this course existed; research duration was not instrumented and duration_seconds=0 records that limitation.
